key_insight: GaOx can function as an effective hole transport layer for 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cells when it is formed by ion exchange during absorber co-evaporation, enabling low-recombination contacts and high voltage.
engineering_relevance: This result supports a simple, heavy-alkali-free contact engineering route to improve chalcopyrite bottom cells for tandem photovoltaics with certified efficiency above 16%.
method: Formed GaOx during co-evaporation of the CuInSe2 absorber via ion exchange
Tested whether Cu addition, Na, and sputtering oxygen flow were needed for conductive GaOx
Characterized the GaOx layer and device performance of optimized solar cells
evidence_signal: The optimized device reached an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified open-circuit voltage of 552 mV.
watch_item: The conductive GaOx behavior appears process-dependent, so reproducibility may require tight control of formation conditions and layer phase composition.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
